What it is

Media

Frame-by-frame

Build prompt

Rebuild this animation 1:1: CRED's deal-of-the-day unlock - the orange deal card flips into a glowing green orb portal, "DEAL UNLOCKED" lands, the percentage morphs upward, and a limited-time-deal sheet slides up with the orb still burning behind it.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
CRED store, dark: "DEAL OF THE DAY" header over an orange deal card (Rs 1,000), "2%" with a gift icon, a gold UNLOCK button, and a sponsored row (Flipkart, Uber) at the bottom. Unlocked state: a luminous green orb card with concentric rings, "DEAL UNLOCKED" and the climbing percentage; final state: a white "limited time deal" sheet with the orb, price (Rs 970), and a Buy Now button.

## Motion spec
Pattern: card-to-portal flip with escalating percentage morph.
- The orange card flips on rotateY (0 -> 180 degrees, 500ms, ease-in-out) revealing the green orb card, which blooms (radial glow 0 -> full, 300ms) as it faces forward.
- "DEAL UNLOCKED" letterspaces in (tracking tightens, opacity 0 -> 1, 300ms); the orb's rings ripple outward on loop (scale 1 -> 1.2 fade, 1.6s).
- The percentage morphs: "2%" -> "2% + 1%" -> "3%" (each swap a vertical roll, 250ms, 400ms apart) while the orb brightens a step per morph.
- Then the deal sheet slides up (spring ~300/18) covering the lower half; the orb shrinks into the sheet's header (shared-element scale + translate, 400ms) and keeps a slow glow pulse (opacity 0.85 -> 1, 1.4s).

## Calibration
- Green means unlocked - nothing green appears before the flip completes.
- The orb is luminous, not flat: layered radial gradients and one slow ring ripple.

## Reduced motion
Card crossfades to the orb card (250ms); percentage swaps without roll; sheet fades up.

## Don't miss
- The gold UNLOCK button dims and stays visible until the sheet covers it - no disappearing chrome mid-sequence.
- The sponsored row at the bottom never animates; it's context, not celebration.
